A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CTSM/CTSM-v research and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F. Corresponding methods, proofs and experiments can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian and Gaussian-mixture experiments, mutual-information estimation, and MNIST density-modeling and sampling results.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds pixel-space MNIST experiments, generated samples, integration-cost measurements and training-failure observations.

M1.justification: The CTSM/CTSM-v objectives, vectorization, probability paths and weighting remain unchanged. Section 6.4 and Appendix F.6 add probability-flow ODE sampling using spatial gradients of integrated time scores, extending the previously described annealed-MCMC inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover distant Gaussians, Gaussian mixtures, Gaussian mutual information and MNIST density modeling/sampling. The added pixel-space and alternative-flow experiments use the same underlying MNIST data and tasks; they change preprocessing and experimental configurations.

E2.justification: TSM remains the comparison method in the matched experiments. Table 1 drops a separately quoted literature TSM result but retains the reproduced TSM baseline. Table 6's weighting-label changes do not introduce different methods.

E3.justification: Added MNIST experiments train directly in pixel space using a residual-block U-Net. Sampling adds probability-flow ODE batches of 64 and ambient-space MCMC in two batches of 50. These supplement the retained experimental protocols; newly disclosed solver settings do not establish changes to earlier runs.

E4.justification: Appendix F.5.2 adds integration-cost analysis, reporting 489.2 evaluations for TSM versus 830.6 for CTSM-v, and exploratory failures with copula/RQ-NSF flows and alternative U-Net configurations. The earlier weighting and bridge-noise sensitivity analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Figures 2–3 retain means and standard deviations over three runs, and Appendix F.3 retains the same seed procedure. No new confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run uncertainty reporting are introduced for MNIST.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains latent-space TSM at 1.30 BPD/347 ms and CTSM-v at 1.26/58 ms. It adds ambient-space CTSM-v at approximately 1.03 BPD/142 ms and unstable TSM at 1103 ms, while removing the quoted 1.33 BPD literature result. These are different-setting additions, not same-setting gains. Figures 2–3 and Tables 2–7 retain their results; new sampling and failure/cost findings supplement them.

T1.justification: Appendix B corrects the mixture identity and missing covariance-scale factors in the general Gaussian time score: v1 Eqs. 43–44 become v3 Eqs. 46 and 52, with supporting derivations. Main theorems and proofs remain unchanged. Newly displayed vectorized formulas in v3 Eqs. 63–64 and 73–75 retain inconsistent factors of D relative to Eq. 54 and the main-text definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: conditional/vectorized time-score learning, faster training with competitive accuracy, stabilization and theoretical error guarantees. Additional MNIST evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds practical qualifications concerning greater integration cost, unstable alternative-flow training and GPU-dependent training dynamics. It hypothesizes a mismatch with network inductive biases and explains why accurate time scores need not yield accurate spatial gradients for sampling. The warning about unreliable BPD normalization already appears in v1.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link and documents SciPy RK45 with relative and absolute tolerances of 1e-6, GPU assignments, timing procedures, checkpoint/instability criteria and sampling batch sizes. These supplement the existing implementation appendix; newly documented settings do not imply that retained experiments changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds connections to Meng et al.'s autoregressive score matching, references supporting sampling-gradient limitations, and diffusion, architecture and software citations. Section 7 more explicitly distinguishes time-score learning from flow/Stein-score approaches. The central positioning against TSM and TRE remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. v3 makes local wording and notation clarifications, adds a Sampling discussion and Impact Statement, subdivides Appendix F.5, and renames F.6. Citation style and several inconsistent labels are also revised.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column presentation to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and repositioning displays. Table 1 gains latent/ambient grouping and a Space column. New pixel-space sample panels appear as Figure 4; the unchanged earlier sample panels become Figure 5 with a corrected caption.

improvement.justification: v3 improves practical validation and transparency through pixel-space MNIST experiments, failure and integration-cost reporting, and added code-access, solver and hardware information. It also corrects the general Gaussian-score formula. These gains are limited by unresolved likelihood-normalization concerns and newly inconsistent D factors in some appendix vectorized formulas; the core methods, guarantees and earlier results remain largely unchanged.
